Early departure to visit Zócalo Square. Holy Mass at Santo Domingo Church, which houses shrines of Our Lady of the Rosary and Our Lady of Covadonga.
After Mass, the excursion continues with visits to Mexico City’s Metropolitan Cathedral, the National Palace and the palace of Archbishop Juan de Zumárraga.
You will then head to Garibaldi Square, where you can enjoy performances by mariachi musicians.





IMPORTANT: A visit to the National Palace cannot be guaranteed because the building is the official residence and workplace of Mexico’s president. This protected government property hosts official events and meetings, so visitor access may be restricted, especially during state ceremonies, meetings and other official engagements.
Access rules for the National Palace may change frequently depending on the president’s schedule and government priorities. For this reason, entry to the building, including its historic murals and other rooms, may be restricted or entirely unavailable to tourists at any time.

You will visit the Metropolitan Cathedral, whose architecture combines Baroque and Neoclassical elements. The National Palace is visited only when access is open. Inside, you may see Diego Rivera’s murals portraying Mexican history from the Aztecs to the twentieth century.

Next are the ruins of Templo Mayor, the temple of ancient Tenochtitlan. According to Aztec legend, an eagle on a cactus with a snake in its beak marked the site where the capital was to be founded. The route follows Paseo de la Reforma toward Chapultepec, which served as a residence for nobility in pre-Hispanic times.

The National Museum of Anthropology presents Mesoamerican cultures, including the Aztec Sun Stone, monumental Olmec stone heads from Tabasco and Veracruz, Teotihuacan frescoes depicting flowers, birds and butterflies, and the diorama and artifacts in the Maya hall.

## Discovering the Panama Canal

We invite your group to [Miraflores](/panama/place/miraflores-locks/) to discover the [Panama Canal](/panama/place/panama-canal/) with an English-speaking guide. We coordinate the group throughout the excursion and include admission tickets to the visitor center.

The excursion takes up to 4 hours. On the seven-day corporate trip, we combine it with lunch and dinner at Mystic India. Transportation and restaurant services are priced separately; departure time is arranged around your group’s schedule.

Duration: 9-10 hours • Pick-up: 9:00 – 9:30 a.m. • Languages: English and Spanish

Today is a celebration of Oaxaca’s spiritual heart, artisanal soul and natural beauty, all in one unforgettable journey. Begin at Mitla, the sacred city of the dead and one of the most important archaeological sites of Mixtec-Zapotec culture. Unlike Monte Albán, Mitla is celebrated for its remarkable geometric stone mosaics, a visual language carved in stone that speaks of life, death and eternity. Continue to Teotitlán del Valle, a picturesque weaving village in the Sierra foothills. Local artisans use natural dyes and time-honored techniques to make handwoven textiles that are as meaningful as they are beautiful. You will see the entire process, from spinning to dyeing and weaving, and meet the families keeping the tradition alive. Next, visit Hierve el Agua, a striking geological formation resembling cascading waterfalls made of mineral deposits. Enjoy panoramic views or dip your feet into its natural scenic pools perched above the valley. Finally, complete the day with a visit to a traditional mezcal distillery, where you will learn about this iconic Oaxacan spirit. Tastings are included.

Tour highlights:

● Discover the spiritual and symbolic richness of Mitla’s sacred ruins.

● Visit a family-run weaving workshop in Teotitlán del Valle.

● Admire the mineral “waterfalls” and panoramic pools at Hierve el Agua.

● Learn the secrets of traditional mezcal and taste it at a local distillery.

● Travel with a certified bilingual guide to discover local culture and stories.

● Spend a full day immersed in nature, tradition and sensory experiences.

Included: Shared transportation, a certified bilingual guide, admission to the archaeological sites and Hierve el Agua, mezcal tasting.

Not included: Meals, tips, personal expenses.
